speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand the swelling in your right knee, can you tell me how long you've had this issue and if you experienced any specific injury or trauma? Also, could you describe the nature of your family members' similar problems?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the knee swell up suddenly or gradually, and was it red, warm, or painful to touch? Also, have you noticed any episodes of excessive bleeding from minor cuts or prolonged bleeding after dental work or circumcision?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Swelling of the right knee. I also have No recent trauma or injury, Familial history of similar symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The previous diagnosis of tuberculosis seems highly unlikely for an 18-month-old with this presentation and family history. I suspect a bleeding disorder like Hemophilia. REQUEST TEST: PT, PTT, and Factor VIII and IX levels.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: PT: 14.0 s, ACT: 52.0 s (prolonged), Factor VIII and IX levels: NOT AVAILABLE

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged activated clotting time (ACT) supports a bleeding diathesis, likely Hemophilia, despite the unavailable factor levels. Can you confirm if the patient has had any other unexplained bruises, nosebleeds, or blood in his urine or stool?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: The parents report no known allergies, normal birth and developmental history for the child.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the patient have a history of easy bruising, frequent nosebleeds, or prolonged bleeding after minor procedures like circumcision? I also need to know if any male relatives on the mother's side have been diagnosed with a bleeding disorder.

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the hemarthrosis, maternal uncle history, and prolonged ACT, I am confident in the diagnosis of Hemophilia A. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A
